parole.testo: From Middle High German komat, kommet, borrowed from Upper Sorbian chomot, from Proto-Slavic *xomǫtъ. Compare Polish chomąto.
From older Nörz, from Upper Sorbian nórc (“mink”), originally meaning "diver", from Proto-Slavic *nora (“den, lair”), *noriti (“to dive, duck”).

parole.significato: A thin, flat cake made from a dough of milk, eggs and either flour or potatoes.
parole.testo: Like Yiddish בלינצע (blintse) (whence English blintz), from Upper Sorbian blinc, blins, plinc, plins (“thin pancake”), dissimilated from mlinc, from Proto-Slavic *mlinъ + *-ьcь, a suffix which this word often bears.
Preisel- + Beere. The former part of the word is borrowed from Upper Sorbian bruslica.

parole.significato: chamber, a room for abode mediocrely furnitured
parole.testo: Depending on the region from either Upper Sorbian komorka or Polish komórka. Doublet of Kammer and Kamera.
